subject: Hosted API: Clarifying geo storage, retention windows, and deletion flow
messages:
From: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@finbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API data residency/retention quick Qs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for walking us through the demo last week. Our legal/security team has a short set of follow-ups for the Hosted API regarding where data is stored, how long we can expect logs/conversation data to persist, and what the deletion process looks like (both API-driven erasures and long-term backups). They want concise answers for our vendor risk assessment.

Can you confirm:
- Do customer request payloads or generated responses ever leave the EU for processing when we select the eu region?
- How long are active request logs kept by default (request/response, metadata, IP logs)?
- If we request a tenant-level purge, what is the end-to-end timeline including KVS, backups, and any asynchronous replications?

Appreciate a short answers doc we can attach to the questionnaire.

Best,
Lena
Security Program Manager
FinBank

FinBank Corporate Security

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@finbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API data residency/retention quick Qs

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below; attaching a short factsheet and a CSV appendix that maps each log type to retention and storage location. If you need formal wording for your questionnaire we can provide an export-friendly JSON snippet for insertion.

1) Regional processing: When you choose the EU region for your workspace, both inference and transient KV/cache processing occur on EU-hosted capacity (we currently run in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for hosted tenants). Persistent logs and analytics derived from requests are configured to remain in-region by default. Cross-region fallbacks only happen under capacity failures and are subject to your region-policy (we can lock fallbacks off).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response payloads (transient): 7 days by default for troubleshooting; configurable down to 0 days for customers who opt for ephemeral mode.
- Request metadata (timestamps, model id, route): 90 days by default for billing/analytics; can be shortened with contract addendum.
- Connection/IP-level logs: 30 days by default to support abuse/incident investigations; can be archived for longer per regulatory needs.

3) Tenant purge / erasure flow:
- API-driven immediate delete: When you call our tenant-erase endpoint, we remove tenant pointers from primary stores and mark related objects for purge. This usually results in logical erasure within 24 hours.
- Background physical deletion: Dependent on storage tier — primary object stores are cleaned within 7 days; cold backups are trimmed in scheduled retention windows and can take up to 90 days to be fully removed from offline media.
- Replication / caches: KV caches and prefix caches are invalidated immediately; replica queues are drained asynchronously and typically empty within 48–72 hours.

Notes:
- We provide a hardened "ephemeral" configuration for customers requiring near-zero retention: it disables request payload logging entirely and keeps only aggregated metrics.
- For customers with strict residency needs, we can disable cross-region failover and provide an attestation.

Attaching the factsheet and appendix now. If you want wording shaped specifically for your vendor portal I'll loop in legal.

Best,
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-factsheet.pdf, finbank-qna-answers-appendix.csv

2) For the "ephemeral" configuration, does that remove all model-level caching (KV caches) and are samples ever used for product analytics/model improvement in that mode?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: security@finbank.com
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API data residency/retention quick Qs

Hi — Ben from Redwood Security & Privacy here, chiming in on the two infra questions: 

1) Backups & key lifecycle: Backups are encrypted with customer-tenant-separated keys managed in our KMS. When a tenant requests a full erasure, we rotate and retire the relevant tenant keys and initiate a scheduled wipe for backups containing that tenant's objects. Because keys are retired, encrypted blobs become non-recoverable even if they persist on offline media. We track key-retirement and correlate it to backup wipe windows; full irrecoverability is generally achieved within 90 days but key retirement is immediate at the time of erasure.

2) Ephemeral mode and analytics: Ephemeral mode disables persistent request payload logging and strips payloads from any analytics pipelines. It also disables storing K/V caches to persistent backing stores — caches are kept only in-memory for the duration of a session. Aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, token counts) is still collected in a non-identifying way to monitor service health. We do not use ephemeral-mode customer data to train or improve models.

If you'd like, Naomi can prepare a short, signed attestation describing the key retirement timeline for your audit packet.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
